Source / variables: MERRA-2 M2T1NXAER; BCCMASS (Buchard et al., 2017; Gelaro et al., 2017; GMAO, 2015; Li et al., 2024; Ou et al., 2022; Randles et al., 2017)
Processing and use: Daily collocated rows were aggregated to the 361 × 576 grid, expressed relative to C₀ = 10⁻⁹ kg m⁻², and transformed with log1p. Monthly means in transformed space define the mean-state target; daily departures define the anomaly target.
Limits on interpretation: Reanalysis-derived proxy for column burden, not independent observational ground truth. A 100-record provenance audit supports consistency with the BCCMASS source field but does not reconstruct every upstream collocation step.

Source / variables: Eight monthly BC sector-group channels for 2022 in the fused analysis dataset, originating from EDGAR v8.1 (Crippa et al., 2026)
Processing and use: The sector-group fields were placed on the common grid during upstream fusion and used in the inventory-only, joint, spatial-control, and bounded-adjustment analyses; they were not the BC column-burden target.
Limits on interpretation: Processed, uncertain bottom-up reference, not emission truth. Native-file conversion, sector aggregation, and remapping were not rerun in this study. The air-pollutant release excludes large-scale savanna and forest fires and land-use, land-use-change, and forestry emissions.

Source / variables: ERA5 hourly fields: t2m (Temp; K), u10 and v10 (Windspeed_U and Windspeed_V; m s⁻¹), blh (BLH; m), and r at 925 hPa (RH; %) (C3S, 2018a, 2018b; Hersbach et al., 2020)
Processing and use: Hourly fields were collocated to POSP locations by temporal interpolation and subsequently aggregated to the common grid. Normalization statistics were estimated only from the 2022 training months and then held fixed. Monthly fields condition the mean-state branch, whereas daily anomalies enter the anomaly branch.
Limits on interpretation: Meteorological predictors represent atmospheric state, not an emission source. Surface pressure was present in the fused files but was not used as a model predictor.

Source / variables: MODIS active-fire latitude, longitude, acquisition date, and channel 21/22 brightness temperature (K) via FIRMS (Giglio et al., 2016; NASA FIRMS, n.d.)
Processing and use: Brightness temperature was summed within each grid cell and acquisition date, transformed with log1p, and used only as an episodic predictor in the anomaly branch.
Limits on interpretation: Brightness indicates fire activity; it is not fire radiative power, plume injection, or a quantitative BC emission flux.

Source / variables: Google Satellite Embedding V1 Annual, bands A00–A63 (Brown et al., 2025; Google Earth Engine, 2025)
Processing and use: Annual embeddings were point-sampled at target grid locations with Earth Engine Reducer.first at a nominal 55-km scale and stored as 64 contextual channels.
Limits on interpretation: Point-sampled, quasi-static surface context; not an area-weighted aggregate, emission inventory, or dynamic atmospheric predictor.

Source / variables: Daily I_380-derived availability; monthly obs_count_map and valid_mask; split labels
Processing and use: Mean-state evaluation required obs_count_map ≥ 5. Training used February, March, May, June, August, and September 2022; November–December 2022 were used for model-selection validation. Formal anomaly runs used 178/61/361 training/validation/2023 samples.
Limits on interpretation: Masks describe coverage of POSP-centered fused source rows, not independent BC quality flags. Models requiring an inventory input in 2023 use the fixed 2022 reference.
